study.title: 1 Kings 4 The administration of Solomon, the peace of the kingdom, and the fame of his wisdom
study.overview: This chapter describes the height of the organization of the kingdom of Solomon. First, it presents its main officers and the administrative structure that supported the government. Then lists the regional governors responsible for supplying the court. He then shows the extent of Israel's dominion, prosperity and peace under his reign. Finally, the text highlights that Solomon's wisdom came from God and that his reputation attracted visitors from many nations.

outline.title: Solomon and his main officers
outline.explanation: The chapter begins by stating that Solomon reigned over all Israel and then lists the heads of his government and his house. The list shows institutional stability and continuity in some positions, in addition to the centralization of real power.

outline.title: The Twelve Governors and the Sustenance of the Royal House
outline.explanation: Twelve regional governors supplied the cut by monthly shifts. The text details its territories, which reveals a broad and efficient administrative system to keep the king and his home.

outline.title: Prosperity, peace and abundant provisions
outline.explanation: Judah and Israel appear numerous and satisfied, and Solomon's dominion is described as extensive and peaceful. The daily provision of the real table and the care of animals show great wealth and organization.

outline.title: The wisdom granted by God and his fame among the nations
outline.explanation: The chapter concludes with the assertion that God gave Solomon wisdom, prudence, and vastness of understanding. This wisdom was expressed in proverbs, songs and knowledge of creation, attracting people from many peoples to hear it.

study.context: The chapter depicts the period when Solomon rules as king over all of Israel. The notes highlight a well-organized cut, with officers, secretaries, administrator of the royal house and responsible for forced labor. There are also district governors in charge of providing the monthly feeding of the court. This picture indicates an administratively centralized and socially prosperous realm with widespread peace and security.
study.theology: The text directly links government, prosperity, and wisdom to the action of God. Solomon is not presented as self-sufficient, but as one to whom God bestows wisdom, prudence, and ample capacity for understanding. The organization of the kingdom shows that God's gifts must be exercised with order and responsibility. At the same time, prosperity and peace can be read as a sign of divine blessing, although the chapter itself does not claim that such conditions eliminate future spiritual risks. The closure prepares a broader reading in which Solomon's fame anticipates, imperfectly, a greater glory, but the text itself here emphasizes above all the excellence granted by God.

scholarViews.insight: The administrator of the royal house was an important officer of the palace, and the one responsible for the tribute administered the forced labor system, an institution that would later be the subject of a complaint in Israel.
The chapter shows Solomon on the throne, confirmed as king over all Israel, in fact exercising the real function with the wisdom that God gave him.
The sixty great cities were fortified cities, with walls and bars of bronze in the gates.

questions: What does the text show about the relationship between God-given wisdom and practical administrative capacity?
How can Solomon's peace and prosperity be signs of blessing without becoming a cause for self-reliance?
How does the fame of Solomon's wisdom challenge our way of evaluating leadership today?
study.practice: This chapter invites the reader to value the wisdom that comes from God and apply it with order, responsibility and service. In practice, this means managing well the resources entrusted, exercising leadership with justice and recognizing that prestige and competence exist to glorify God, not to feed pride. It is also a call to seek wisdom above wealth and appearance of success, remembering that true spiritual greatness is evident in faithfulness and fear of the Lord.
